{{Quote|Do not fail me again!|Rezi Soresh|<ref name="Rebel Force: Trapped">''[[Rebel Force: Trapped]]''</ref>}}
[[Commander/Legends|Commander]] '''Rezi Soresh''' was an [[Officer/Legends|officer]] in the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and the man who [[Project Omega|created]] [[X-1 (assassin)|X-1]], [[X-2]], [[X-3]], [[X-4]], [[X-5]], [[X-6]], and [[X-7]] in an attempt to create the perfect [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]]. Of the seven, X-7 was the only one to survive his training. Soresh was hired by the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] to kill the [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] who had destroyed the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]]. When he [[Battle of Belazura|failed]], he fled [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] wrath and [[Unidentified dead red moon|settled]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. During his [[Battle of the Sixela system|attempt]] to turn young Skywalker into his own assassin and gain his revenge, Soresh was gunned down by [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]].

==Biography==
===Assassin program===
Soresh, a [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] took seven men and forced them into a [[Project Omega|brutal reconditioning program]] designed to turn them into mindless servants. Using a system of drugs which he perfected, he usurped their personalities. They were then pitted against each other until only one remained. X-7 had become the perfect [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] and was utterly tied to his master, Soresh, and went on to perform flawlessly in every task..<ref name="Rebel Force: Target" />

===Vendetta===
By [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], Soresh was suffering from the perceived insult of having been placed in a lower position for a man of his abilities. Upon meeting [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], Rezi planned on destroying him and rising in the [[Palpatine/Legends|Emperor's]] eyes. Through dubious intelligence sources, he discovered that the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] Luke Skywalker was actually Vader's son. Soresh wanted to kill him and discredit Vader, who was also searching for the young Rebel. Soresh sent X-7 after Skywalker with the exhortation not to fail him.<ref name="Rebel Force: Target" />

During the course of the hunt, Soresh would often contact X-7 and ask for a status update.<ref name="Rebel Force: Hostage">''[[Rebel Force: Hostage]]''</ref> X-7 failed several times to kill Skywalker despite gaining his trust under the alias of Tobin Elad.<ref name="Rebel Force: Hostage" />

Soresh eventually grew angry with X-7, and recalled him for additional reconditioning. But his efforts only added to the strained mental state of X-7, who had begun to question the actions of his master.<ref name="Rebel Force: Trapped" />

When the Rebels set up a trap for X-7 on [[Belazura]], he fell for it. They used [[Lune Oddo Divinian]], a mercenary hired by X-7, to masquerade as X-7's brother and reveal his real name: [[Trever Flume]]. Eventually, X-7 had to face a final choice between his potential past and serving his master. X-7 stunned Divinian and joined the Imperial assault against Rebel infiltrators. The battle ended with Soresh's finest assassin dead.<ref name="Rebel Force: Trapped" />

===Endgame===
Lord Vader had discovered Soresh's attempts to usurp power and ordered his capture. An Imperial [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] confronted Soresh and told him Vader was coming to deal with the arrogant commander personally. Panicked, Soresh initiated his backup escape plans while the Lieutenant waited outside. By the time Vader arrived, Soresh had completed his escape. When he discovered Soresh had fled, Vader [[Telekinesis/Legends#Force Choke|executed]] the Lieutenant for his failure.<ref name="Rebel Force: Trapped" />

Soresh spent the next twenty-seven days fleeing Vader in backward systems in his [[CloakShape fighter/Legends|CloakShape fighter]]. Stumbling upon the [[Sixela system/Legends|Sixela system]], Soresh landed and set about using his remaining influence to achieve his revenge against Luke Skywalker.<ref name="Rebel Force: Uprising" />

When the [[Heroes of Yavin/Legends|Heroes of Yavin]] were participating in a [[Mission to Nyemari]], a [[Unidentified Glymphid messenger|Glymphid]] approached Skywalker to deliver a message. It was a [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]] of Soresh asking for Skywalker to meet him in the Sixela system, and threatening to kill a [[Endeavor (Arkanian starship)|colony vessel]] full of over 100 passengers if he didn't comply. As a measure of his power, Soresh used some sort of delayed [[Poison/Legends|poison]] and killed the messenger in front of Skywalker.<ref name="Rebel Force: Uprising" />

Skywalker knew he needed to turn himself in, but his friends would not let him go alone. Just before the deadline was going to expire, they landed on Soresh's [[Unidentified dead red moon|moon]] in the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']]. [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] stepped out and greeted a [[Rezi Soresh (impostor)|man identifying himself as Soresh]]. Then, two [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing starfighters]] swept over the planet and attacked the compound, knocking out the [[Laser turret/Legends|laser turrets]]. Solo then shot the impostor. After the Rebels landed, a series of [[Mine/Legends|mines]] started exploding amongst the hostages. The Rebels waded into the mob to attempt to rescue them, and were captured.

Solo and [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] were placed in a jail cell guarded by individuals with no emotions, more examples of Soresh's handiwork. Meanwhile, Soresh had taken Skywalker for himself and planned on turning him into a perfect, [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] assassin. Over a two-week period, Soresh broke down Skywalker's defenses. Skywalker came close to capitulating, but he knew his friends were counting on him, and he faked his emotions and responses.<ref name="Rebel Force: Uprising" />

When Solo and Organa next saw Skywalker, he appeared to be a mindless servant of Soresh. When Skywalker was ordered to execute his comrades, he was given a blaster, and aimed it at his friends. Suddenly, there came a [[Aridinian folk music|piercing screech]], and his shot went wild. The [[Droid/Legends|droid]] duo, [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] and [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] had been left behind during the original raid and they staged a diversion. Solo, Organa, and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] took cover behind rocks. A guard was about to execute Solo when Skywalker shot him, revealed his deception while Solo tried to convince him to escape. Skywalker would not leave without discovering Soresh's plan. He asked a favor from Solo: shoot him in the shoulder to make it appear he was still Soresh's servant. When Skywalker woke up, he faked his emotions of failing his master. Soresh forgave him, but still punished him for his failure. The other Rebels had escaped and were later met by the [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] [[Lune Oddo Divinian|Div]] and Organa's longtime guardian, [[Ferus Olin]]. The two were on an unsanctioned reconnaissance mission.<ref name="Rebel Force: Uprising" />

Soresh had planted evidence to the Rebellion that [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] and the [[Imperial High Command/Legends|Imperial High Command]] were going to meet in the Sixela system in with only a small guard. [[General/Legends|General]] [[Jan Dodonna/Legends|Jan Dodonna]] committed the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet]] to attacking the contingent. Soresh also contacted Vader to draw him into his trap. Soresh wanted to take his revenge at once. Through his contacts, he acquired his trump card: [[resonance torpedo]]es, which he would use to destroy the [[Fleet/Legends|fleets]].<ref name="Rebel Force: Uprising" />

When the Alliance Fleet reverted from [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]], they quickly discovered it was a trap, as a large Imperial fleet arrived. Soresh offered Skywalker his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] back if he launched the torpedoes. Instead, Skywalker turned on him. Soresh launched the torpedoes at the sun, and then fled. Skywalker's companions arrived but were unable to stop the launch. Meanwhile, Darth Vader had landed and was looking for Soresh. Skywalker used a [[Mind trick/Legends|mind trick]] to subdue the rest of Soresh's guards, allowing them to escape, and then Solo and Skywalker joined the [[Battle of the Sixela system|battle]] in [[Space warfare/Legends|space]].

The torpedoes hit the sun and started a chain reaction, which would end in 40 minutes. The two fleets fled, and Skywalker returned to the moon to rescue the remaining hostages, and Olin sacrificed himself to engage Vader. He was soon [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|struck down]] by Vader and was finally at rest.

Their work finished, the Rebels boarded the ''Falcon''. They were stopped by Soresh, who attempted to shoot Skywalker, but Solo shot down the man, ending his plans. The Rebels fled the system before the sun exploded and wiped out all trace of Soresh's work.<ref name="Rebel Force: Uprising" />

==Personality and traits==
Soresh was an ambitious man, and yet, to many others he appeared only to be a lackey.<ref name="Rebel Force: Target" /> He was angry that he was put in a minor position and plotted to gain favor with the Emperor.<ref name="Rebel Force: Trapped" /> He would tolerate no failure from his those under him and would go so far as to let them kill each other. Soresh was smart enough to plan for all contingencies and had a backup plan in case of failure. Even during his exile, he was able to rebuild his power base.<ref name="Rebel Force: Uprising" />

Soresh was a meticulous man who liked to be prepared. He studied the blueprints of every building he planned to spend significant time in to make sure he always had an escape route. And he never arrived on a planet without making sure that he had a second ship on standby for an alternate transportation.<ref name="Rebel Force: Uprising" />

==Behind the scenes==
Rezi Soresh is one of the primary antagonists in the ''[[Star Wars: Rebel Force]]'' series by [[Alex Wheeler]]. Those books represent his only appearance in ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], although the series was included in the [[2012]] reference book ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'', which offers plot summaries for all ''Star Wars'' literary works.
